verdict: not keyed: 42 signs in 11 groups do not take the record's plaintext (bayt 1, 48 letters, or bayt 2, 44) as a simple substitution; no consistent alignment found
notes: Rows 3v l.12 (whole width), 3v l.13 (the segmenter box covers only x 723-1470; the row runs to the margin, x ~135), 4r l.1, and 2 signs at the right of 4r l.2 before 'فاحضرها'. By eye 14+15+11+2 = 42 signs (record 16+18+12+2 = 48), 11 dividers (record 11; the stem at the left end of 3v l.12 has faded dots and is a divider, not a sign). Group lengths 5,3,3,3,4,5,2,4,2,4,7: 11 groups = the 11 words of bayt 1 (الشيخ ... الاوصاف), and the first and last groups fit its first and last words by length and pattern (last group S23 S21 S23 S24 S25 S23 S26 has the same sign in places 1, 3 and 6, as ا in الاوصاف), but the middle groups do not (3,3,3,4,5,2,4,2,4 against 2,3,3,3,7,3,7,4,4) and the key breaks: S21 would be ل (place 2 of الاوصاف) but stands third in the 4-sign group where bayt 1 has كامل (ل fourth). The end also fits bayt 2's last words من جملة الالطاف (2,4,7, with S21 = S24 = ل), but the groups before them do not fit bayt 2 either. A search over both bayts (groups matched to words in order, skips allowed, one letter per shape) finds at most 25 of 42 signs placed, by chance-level fits. The compiler says the patron made the riddle 'with dropping of the ya' (3v l.10, وحذف الياء) and that the shaykh brought it to him; the sign forms are letter-like (لى, ك, ل, س, ص, ع, ط shapes, numerals ٨ ٩), which may point to a system other than one sign per letter. Left unkeyed; plaintext reading of 4r l.4: the third word of the second half reads لان on the page (lam-alif, then a tail with one dot above) where the record has لدن.
